message.content:
Lions (family Felidae) and zebras (family Equidae) belong to two different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively.  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which gave rise to both of those orders.  

That ancestor lived roughly **70 million years ago** (in the late Cretaceous/early Paleocene) and was a small, insect‑eating mammal that eventually diversified into the many lineages that make up modern carnivores, odd‑toed ungulates, even‑toed ungulates, bats, and whales.
